Tooltip.Stale: Today's weather hasn't been rolled yet. It will be once a GM is online.
Tooltip.StaleGM: Today's weather hasn't been rolled yet.
Tooltip.Forecast: Tomorrow (only you see this): {condition}, high {high}, low {low}, {wind}

clear.Name: Clear
clear.Hint: Not a cloud in the sky.

overcast.Name: Overcast
overcast.Hint: A grey lid of cloud, but dry.

heavyRain.Name: Heavy rain
heavyRain.Hint: A downpour. Roads turn to mud.

sleet.Name: Sleet
sleet.Hint: Half-frozen rain that stings and soaks.

iceStorm.Name: Ice storm
iceStorm.Hint: Freezing rain that glazes everything in ice.

blizzard.Name: Blizzard
blizzard.Hint: Driving snow and a howling wind.

duststorm.Name: Dust storm
duststorm.Hint: A wall of blowing sand and dust.

fog.Name: Fog
fog.Text: The area is lightly obscured, and the thickest patches are heavily obscured.

heavyPrecipitation.Name: Heavy precipitation
heavyPrecipitation.Text: Everything in it is lightly obscured, and creatures have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

heavyRain.Name: Heavy rain
heavyRain.Text: Puts out open flames, and gives disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing.

slipperyIce.Name: Ice
slipperyIce.Text: Iced-over ground is difficult terrain. A creature moving onto it for the first time on a turn makes a DC 10 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check or falls prone.

dust.Name: Blowing sand
dust.Text: The area is lightly obscured, and creatures have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

strongWind.Name: Strong wind
strongWind.Text: Disadvantage on ranged weapon attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing. It puts out open flames and disperses fog. Flying without magic is nearly impossible: a flying creature must land at the end of its turn or fall.

extremeHeat.Name: Extreme heat
extremeHeat.Text: At 100°F (38°C) or more, a creature without drinkable water makes a Constitution saving throw at the end of each hour, DC 5 for the first hour and 1 higher for each hour after, gaining a level of exhaustion on a failure. Medium or heavy armor or heavy clothing gives disadvantage. Resistance or immunity to fire damage, or being adapted to hot climates, means it succeeds automatically.

extremeCold.Name: Extreme cold
extremeCold.Text: At 0°F (-18°C) or less, a creature exposed to it makes a DC 10 Constitution saving throw at the end of each hour, gaining a level of exhaustion on a failure. Cold weather gear, resistance or immunity to cold damage, or being adapted to cold climates means it succeeds automatically.

Menu.ShowOnScene: Show the weather on this scene's map
Menu.HideOnScene: Stop showing the weather on this scene's map
Menu.WhisperChat: Whisper the weather to the GMs

Dialog.Title: Weather
Dialog.Intro: The climate and season decide what weather is likely. Rolls follow on from the day before, so warm spells and wet weeks carry on for a while.
Dialog.TodayHint: Roll new weather replaces today's weather with a roll for the climate and season above. Save keeps what's set here as today's weather, if you changed it. Either way tomorrow's weather follows on from today's.

Notify.Failed: Primal Weather couldn't save the weather. The console (F12) has the details.

climate.Name: Climate
climate.Hint: Where the party is. Temperate: four seasons, rain all year, snow in winter. Coastal: mild, foggy and windy. Mountain: cold, windy and snowy, with summer storms. Arctic: bitter cold and long winters. Desert: scorching days, cold nights, dust storms and rare rain. Tropical: hot all year, with a wet summer and a dry winter. Changing it rolls tomorrow's forecast again; today's weather stays until you roll it again.

season.Name: Season
season.Hint: Read from dnd5e's calendar by default (Gregorian, Greyhawk, Harptos or Khorvaire), changing gradually through the year. Pick a season to fix it instead, for a calendar without seasons or a different hemisphere.

autoRoll.Name: Roll new weather each day
autoRoll.Hint: When the calendar reaches a new day, the GM's client rolls that day's weather, following on from the day before. Jumping ahead several days rolls each of them, and going back in time shows the weather those days had. Turn off to keep the weather until you roll it yourself.

visibility.Name: Who sees the weather
visibility.Hint: Everyone sees the weather bar under the calendar, or only the GM.

sceneEffects.Name: Weather on the map
sceneEffects.Hint: Show the weather with Foundry's own effects (rain, rain storm, fog, snow, blizzard) on scene maps. Mark a scene as outdoors from the weather bar's ⋮ menu. A scene with its own weather set in Scene Config keeps it, and Suppress Weather regions still work.
sceneEffects.All: Every scene, unless turned off for it

announce.Name: Announce new weather in chat
announce.Hint: Post a card in chat when the weather changes: each new day, and whenever the GM rolls or sets it.

showBar.Name: Show the weather bar
showBar.Hint: Show today's weather under the calendar (this browser only).

units.Name: Temperature units
units.Hint: How temperatures are shown (this browser only).

rollRules.Name: Weather rules apply to rolls
rollRules.Hint: On outdoor scenes (the ones showing the weather: the weather bar's ⋮ menu → Show the weather on this scene's map, or every scene when Weather on the map is set to Every scene): with Primal Status on, heavy rain, heavy snow, fog, blowing sand and strong wind give Disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks, and strong wind on ranged weapon attacks, with the reason shown so a player can roll normally when the check doesn't rely on that sense. In extreme heat or cold the GM gets a whispered reminder each hour that saving throws are due.

RollRules.HourPassed: An hour has passed outdoors on {scene}.
